description: Firsthand triage of every Slither finding that touches prototype/vnext-kernel/contracts. Keyed by SEMANTIC IDENTITY (scanner-finding-identity.ts semanticId): a sha256 over detector + per-element file, element chain and signature + the detector message with line references normalised away. The key contains NO line numbers, offsets or spans, so a finding that only moves keeps its identity and its adjudication. The v1 locator key (<check>|<sorted filename:firstLine>) is RETAINED per entry under locators, together with every superseded locator, because it is how a finding is found in a specific checkout and because deleting it would discard history. fingerprints.narrow covers the node elements Slither actually flagged and is absent when a finding has none; fingerprints.broad covers every element including the enclosing function. A narrow difference PROVES the flagged construct changed; a broad-only difference proves the surrounding source changed and requires re-adjudication without asserting more than that. generate-scanner-evidence.ts --validate fails on any untriaged finding, any triage entry matching no current finding, any ambiguous identity, any fingerprint drift, and any scanner-input scope mismatch between the declared subjects.

keyedAt.fingerprintNote: fingerprints.narrow (node elements only) and fingerprints.broad (every element) are computed with normaliseSolidity, a STRING-AWARE scanner. The regex it replaces stripped comment markers wherever they appeared, including inside string literals, so a URL, revert string or ABI signature containing a double slash had everything after it erased -- two revisions differing only there produced the same fingerprint and a real change would have been reported UNCHANGED. fingerprintAlgorithm names the current scheme and the generator refuses a triage whose algorithm it does not implement, so comment handling can never change without the stored values being re-derived.

381192ae61db95b6926fff7d7d422e3ff169f86f.rationale: verify refuses an attestation whose deadline has passed, `block.timestamp > deadline` (prototype copy line 89). The deadline is the attestor-chosen replay bound the class documents as the SOLE DIRECT one, with replay otherwise bounded transitively by the vault nonce inside the attested digest; in this kernel that is _consume's nonce and deadline over the same digest. Clock skew (0 s on post-merge L1, ~15 s forward-only historically, up to 1,800 s of OP-Stack sequencer drift) can only move the instant an already-signed attestation stops being accepted. It cannot create an attestation, change the immutable attestor, or make a statement authorise a digest it does not name, and the kernel's own nonce and deadline still bound the action. Pinned by the production test/ImmutableAttestationPQCVerifier.test.ts ('rejects an expired attestation'). Lane SD-11: byte-identical copy of the production Generation-1 verifier class.

53e7c99e40a24565edcedacc1d8e61c053ebca4e.rationale: _requireIncomingPossession reads no clock: there is no block.timestamp, deadline or expiresAt reference anywhere in its body (verified at the source subject over lines 753-803), and the comparison Slither prints -- `popDigest.recover(c.newEcdsaPop) != expectedSigner` -- has no clock operand. The report is the node-context taint described in the W2S record: the function is reached from rotateCredential (line 954) and executeRecovery (line 1503), both of which do read the clock, and Slither evaluates data dependency in NODE context with field-insensitive struct dependency, so every later comparison in the callee is flagged. The clock argument therefore rests on those two callers' own entries, not on this one.

545868d5fa4442836b557762849165206695d5aa.rationale: ImmutableAttestationPQCVerifier.verify destructures ECDSA.tryRecover's three return values as (recovered, error, ) and uses BOTH recovered and error in its return statement, `error == ECDSA.RecoverError.NoError && recovered == attestor` (prototype copy line 106). Only the third value, OpenZeppelin's error argument, is discarded by the blank identifier: it is diagnostic detail about WHICH recovery failure occurred, and every failure it could describe already makes error != NoError, so the function returns false either way. Identical pattern to EcdsaBackedVerifier (entry d642d2aa). Lane SD-11: the file is a byte-identical copy of contracts/verifiers/ImmutableAttestationPQCVerifier.sol, the Generation-1 verifier class, and its refusal path is exercised by the production test/ImmutableAttestationPQCVerifier.test.ts ('rejects an attestation from the wrong attestor').

67105f17ea8353a8c4e9f04f1b2130bc46ff3858.rationale: cancelRecovery's only clock read is the _recoveryIsLive() gate at VaultKernelPrototype.sol:1387, adjudicated under the timestamp entry keyed :742,:743. The comparison Slither prints for this function, recovery.challengesUsed >= CHALLENGE_LIMIT (:1255), has no timestamp-derived operand: challengesUsed is written only by the += 1 in this function, the carry-forward in initiateRecovery and the whole-struct delete in executeRecovery (I-RECOVERY-CHALLENGE-EPOCH). It is reported because the timestamp detector evaluates data dependency in NODE context: after the _recoveryIsLive() internal call, whose return value depends on block.timestamp and on the recovery struct, the node-context dependency set of the recovery storage reference includes block.timestamp (probed with the pinned Slither's is_dependent: node-context true, function-context false, W2S_SCANNER_TRIAGE_RECORD.md section 5.2); the identical comparison at e6964aeb, gated by the raw recovery.active byte, produced no report. What the clock decides here is WHETHER a credential challenge is admitted: while live (t < expiresAt) the challenge consumes one budget unit and clears request authority; once expired it is refused with NoRecovery before any nonce or budget is touched (test/W2RecoveryLifecycle.test.ts B1-B3 'challenge' probes; mutant M-K9-expired-request-still-challengeable). Bounded skew (0 s on post-merge L1, ~15 s forward-only PoW-era, 1,800 s OP-Stack sequencer drift) can move that instant by seconds against a 14-day window and can neither refund nor exceed the budget, so it hands the credential no capability beyond the bounded challenge that architecture section 22 D1 already prices (I-VETO-BOUND).

6e4c498d3bd894e9f50a1287e2f5d16935a6fb9c.rationale: egress declares `uint256 moved` with no explicit initializer, so it holds Solidity's zero value until assigned; Slither flags it because not every path assigns it. The native-value branch (asset == address(0)) assigns moved = address(this).balance explicitly. The ERC-20 branch assigns moved = before - remaining only inside if (before != 0): after a positive source balance, the transfer call, and an observed balance decrease (remaining >= before reverts TransferFailed). When before == 0 the vault holds none of the asset, no transfer is attempted, and leaving moved == 0 is the intended semantic result, so emit Egressed(asset, destination, moved) reports the correct zero movement rather than reading an indeterminate value (Solidity locals have none). Pinned by test/ScannerAdjudicationPremises.test.ts P-148: a bound vault egressing an ERC-20 it holds none of succeeds, moves nothing, emits Egressed(asset, destination, 0) and changes no other kernel state or balance; its positive control shows the same revert-on-transfer token WITH a balance is reached and refused. Re-adjudicated by the scanner-premise correction lane: the previous rationale claimed exhaustive assignment, which the ERC-20 branch never had; the classification is unchanged.

951fd542bfda583b589d5977d56cd31a7c66129b.rationale: deployVault CREATE2-deploys a fresh clone (Clones.cloneDeterministicWithImmutableArgs, an internal library call) pointing at this factory's immutable implementation, then calls that clone's known initialize(g, pqKey), and emits VaultDeployed only after initialize returns successfully; genesisSalt before it is a pure call to the implementation. initialize is NOT free of external interaction: since SD-11 (b058715b) it sets _initialized = true first and then calls _requireAdmissibleVerifier(g.verifier), one external view call (STATICCALL) to IKernelVerifierAuthority.isAdmissibleVerifier on the verifier authority this factory generation binds immutably and the clone reads from its own code. The static execution context propagates through every frame that authority opens, so an authority calling back into deployVault cannot execute CREATE2, SSTORE, LOG or any other state-changing operation: it cannot deploy a second vault or emit a second VaultDeployed, and a callback into the half-built clone's initialize is refused AlreadyInitialized because the flag was set before the call. The factory itself holds no mutable state (three immutables, no storage), so nothing it owns can be corrupted across the call. Pinned by test/ScannerAdjudicationPremises.test.ts P-349: a hostile authority's reentrant deployVault frame halts with StateChangeDuringStaticCall, no second vault or event appears, the factory is unchanged and the outer clone keeps its genesis; positive controls show the identical callback deploys a vault from an ordinary CALL frame, and that a kernel mutant making the admission call with CALL does reenter. Re-adjudicated by the scanner-premise correction lane: the previous rationale's premise about initialize predates SD-11 and is false on this kernel; the classification is unchanged.

a40b08ff68c3fb8b1713973bc3a5704ad459cc5e.rationale: executeRecovery gates on block.timestamp < r.executableAt (TooEarly; RECOVERY_DELAY = 7 days) and, CHANGED BY W2 (SD-9e, Recovery Amendment section 3), on block.timestamp >= r.expiresAt (Expired; RECOVERY_EXPIRY = 14 days): the half-open window [executableAt, expiresAt) that makes execution consistent with _recoveryIsLive(). At expiresAt-1 execution, both cancellations and the migration block all hold; at expiresAt and expiresAt+1 execution reverts Expired, both cancellations revert NoRecovery consuming no nonce and no budget, migration binds, and a fresh initiation is admitted with its own full delay (test/W2RecoveryLifecycle.test.ts B1-B4 and G3, each probe mined at its asserted instant). Re-adjudicated in Lane W2S rather than carried forward: the only difference the change makes to the timestamp argument is that the last authorised instant moved from expiresAt to expiresAt-1, removing the one-second window in which the pre-W2 kernel executed a request every other consumer already treated as expired. Validator discretion is bounded: post-merge L1 timestamps are fixed per 12-second slot (no proposer discretion; the only lever is inclusion), PoW-era skew was at most ~15 s and forward-only (a lagging timestamp cost the miner difficulty and was corrected by the next honest block), and OP-Stack L2 sequencer drift is bounded at 1,800 s relative to the L1 origin -- at most 0.3% of RECOVERY_DELAY and 0.15% of RECOVERY_EXPIRY. Skew moves both bounds of every principal's window together, reads no signature, quorum or possession check, and therefore cannot execute an unmatured or expired request, cannot bypass the quorum that alone creates an active request (initiateRecovery), and cannot reset the challenge epoch, whose only reset is this function's own delete recovery after a successful, authorised execution. Mutant M-K9-expiry-inclusive-off-by-one (> here, <= in the predicate) is killed by the B-series boundary property (test/W2RecoveryLifecycleMutations.test.ts).

dab74d67c746fea1e0973f8f476caae989097c3b.rationale: _recoveryIsLive() IS I-RECOVERY-EFFECTIVE-LIVENESS (Recovery Amendment section 3): a request holds authority on the HALF-OPEN window [executableAt, expiresAt), so active && block.timestamp < recovery.expiresAt is the one deliberate clock read that every recovery-lifecycle decision consults -- initiateRecovery's live-overwrite refusal, cancelRecovery, cancelRecoveryByQuorum and bindMigration; executeRecovery mirrors it with >= expiresAt. Adjudicated independently in Lane W2S (W2S_SCANNER_TRIAGE_RECORD.md section 5), not inherited from the older timestamp entries. (1) The predicate decides only WHETHER an already-authorised act lands, never WHO is authorised: no signature, quorum or possession check reads the clock, so no authority cut in AUTHORITY.md section 4 moves with it. (2) Every consumer applies the same inequality, so there is no block in which the request is executable but not cancellable, or cancellable but not executable; test/W2RecoveryLifecycle.test.ts B1-B3 pins all five consumers at expiresAt-1 (live: execution succeeds, both cancellations succeed, migration is blocked, initiation is refused as overwrite), expiresAt and expiresAt+1 (expired: Expired / NoRecovery with nothing consumed / migration binds / fresh initiation admitted), and G3 pins the three instants as consecutive blocks of one world. (3) Validator discretion is bounded: post-merge L1 timestamps are fixed per 12-second slot (no proposer discretion; the only lever is inclusion), PoW-era skew was at most ~15 s and forward-only, and OP-Stack L2 sequencer drift is bounded at 1,800 s relative to the L1 origin -- at most 0.15% of RECOVERY_EXPIRY (14 days) and 0.3% of RECOVERY_DELAY (7 days); a forward skew can only make a request expire EARLY, shrinking every principal's window together, never extend it. (4) Consequently skew cannot refund the challenge epoch (challengesUsed is written only by the += 1 in cancelRecovery, the carry-forward in initiateRecovery and the whole-struct delete in executeRecovery), cannot bypass the quorum (only initiateRecovery creates an active request), cannot execute an expired request (t >= expiresAt reverts, and expiry is defined in the same clock the request was created in), cannot overwrite a live request (initiateRecovery reverts BadState while live; a fresh request over an EXPIRED one is by design not an overwrite, and the quorum could in any case have cancelled its own live request) and cannot lower any cut. Mutants M-K9-expiry-inclusive-off-by-one, M-K9-expired-request-still-challengeable, M-K9-expired-request-still-quorum-cancellable, M-K9-expired-request-blocks-migration, M-K9-expired-request-blocks-initiation, M-K9-live-overwrite-allowed and M-K9-expiry-refunds-budget are all killed (test/W2RecoveryLifecycleMutations.test.ts).

6182a341019adb4da8925fa07ed84ee900dfa9e0.rationale: This comparison IS the invariant. I-CONTAINMENT-BUDGET (T0) is stated on wall-clock time, so enterContainment's two-start rule compares block.timestamp with a stored episode start plus CONTAINMENT_WINDOW (30 days) by design — lane SD-2's remediation, replacing the tumbling rollover that entry 3c76da07 (retired at this subject) covered with the same day-scale argument. Timestamp slack (0 s on post-merge L1, ~15 s forward-only historically, up to ~30 min of OP-Stack sequencer drift) can move only WHICH block sits at the 30-day boundary; it cannot admit a third episode inside a window nor refuse one whose second-most-recent start is a window old by more than the slack, and the rule is half-open by design (a start exactly W old is legal). The `previous != 0` leg is the no-history sentinel, not a time comparison. Pinned at exact instants on both sides of every boundary by test/Sd2RollingContainmentRemediation.test.ts sections 1-2 and observed independently by the campaign oracle G-CONTAINMENT-ROLLING-BUDGET.

508db3a7ee1aa7a068df52fbf8148d654dbe59ef.rationale: A view. containmentWindowStart() reports the rolling window's origin, block.timestamp - CONTAINMENT_WINDOW; the flagged comparison `nowTs > CONTAINMENT_WINDOW` is the underflow clamp to 0 while a chain is younger than one window, unreachable on any live network. No authorization path reads this function: the getter survives only so the ABI's former per-epoch origin keeps a truthful rolling meaning (SD-2 remediation).

f1d14a042240dc7260159b3d84d1daefad17e5d2.rationale: A view. containmentUsedInWindow() reports the contained seconds inside [now - CONTAINMENT_WINDOW, now) from the three most recent episode starts; the flagged comparisons are the same underflow clamp and the `containedUntil == 0` no-episode sentinel (containedUntil is only ever written as block.timestamp + CONTAINMENT_MAX, so 0 is unreachable as a real expiry). No authorization path reads it; it exists so the ABI's former per-epoch counter keeps a truthful rolling meaning (SD-2 remediation). Its value is pinned against the observed episode list in test/Sd2RollingContainmentRemediation.test.ts 3.3.

63e308eaf4627d8e9eaf7c20bb0e10871c3e2359.rationale: Pure interval arithmetic: the seconds of the episode [start, start + CONTAINMENT_MAX) that fall inside [from, to), plus the `start == 0` no-episode sentinel. The detector taints every comparison because `to` is the caller's block.timestamp. Private, pure, reachable only from the containmentUsedInWindow view; on no authorization path (SD-2 remediation).
